trace.question:
I tried to look up the payments service, but the service registry rejected the name — "payments" isn't a recognized service identifier, and the deployment listing came back empty. I don't want to guess a service name and risk acting on the wrong system.

Could you tell me the exact service name as it's registered (e.g., is it `payments-service`, `payment-api`, or something else)? Once I have that, I'll pull its release history, roll back to the last version that was healthy in production, and file the SEV2 incident.

trace.message: It's payments-worker - the API errors are downstream of the worker.

trace.text: It's payments-worker - the API errors are downstream of the worker.

args.summary: payments-worker v3.4.0 (deployed this morning) is unhealthy in all production regions with an 18% error rate, causing downstream API errors in the payments service. Rolled back to last known-healthy release v3.3.0 across all regions.
args.title: payments-worker v3.4.0 deploy causing elevated error rates and downstream API failures

trace.final:
Done. Here's what happened:

1. **Identified the bad release** — `payments-worker` was on **v3.4.0** (this morning's deploy) across all three production regions, unhealthy with an **18% error rate**. **v3.3.0** was the last release marked healthy.

2. **Rolled back** — `payments-worker` rolled back to **v3.3.0** in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), rollout verified.

3. **Confirmed recovery** — the service is now **healthy** with error rate down to **0.2%**.

4. **Opened incident** — **INC-0001 (SEV2)** documenting the v3.4.0 deploy causing downstream API errors and the rollback to v3.3.0; on-call has been paged.

One note: no change-manager approval was needed since v3.3.0 had already been healthy in production. You may want to notify whoever shipped v3.4.0 to root-cause it before it goes out again.
